notes: A plain residential grid in the Sunset, 1964 sheet p06: four columns of long blocks running across the page (x about 4025-4252, 4276-4505, 4528-4758, 4781-5010) in nine rows (block tops at about y 3605, 3717, 3830, 3946, 4059, 4173, 4287, 4403, 4520), streets about 25-30 px wide between them, all blocks plain rectangles (no alleys, no notches). 36 polygons, one per printed block; no open polygons: the box holds no ground without an outline of its own and no blank paper (the mapped ground ends at the heavy line at x 5017-5025, beyond the box; col 4's own right side is at x 5004-5010, also beyond it). Box as given (4040, 3620, 940, 940): its left side cuts the first column of blocks (their left side is at x 4025-4030), its top cuts the first row (tops at y 3601-3608), its right side the fourth column and its bottom the last row; those blocks end on the box edge. How the sides were placed: ink is darker than 138; for each block side, every 2 px along its middle, a scan from 4 px inside the block's own thin line outward to its first ink and through it gives the outermost ink px of that line (where the run was wider than 5 px, a heavy border touching it, the thin line's 3 px width was taken from its inner edge); a straight line was fitted to these points (points more than 2 px off dropped) and corners are the intersections of neighbouring sides. Set by hand from the ink where the scan could not run: the top of the row-8 block in column 1 (y 4406, the heavy border in the street lies 12 px above it), the left side of column 3 in rows 8 and 9 (x 4532 and 4533, where the R-3 lettering lies on it at (4524-4560, 4400-4450)), the left side of column 2 in row 9 (x 4281); and two tops moved 1 px to the ink after an automatic check (row 5 column 1 at its left end, y 4061; row 8 column 1 at its right end, y 4405). Then checked block by block on 2x-4x ruled close-ups and on the labels picture. The grid is turned about 0.3 degrees on the scan, and the street between rows 8 and 9 (y about 4480-4535) narrows and slants going right: the row-8 blocks' bottoms and row-9 blocks' tops in columns 2 and 3 slope by 5-8 px across one block, and the polygons follow that slope. Heavy zoning borders: one runs along that street (y 4492-4518, about 9 px thick) and short pieces lie in other streets (y 4389-4394 x 4040-4250; y 4273-4278 x 4280-4500); these are street. Many run THROUGH blocks and do not split them (one polygon per block): x 4205-4213 down column 1, x 4062-4067 and the C-1 district box at (4040-4120, 3700-3820) in column 1, x 4305-4321 and 4461-4475 down column 2, and the R-2 enclosure whose top runs in the street at y 4273-4278 and whose bottom crosses the column-2 block of row 7 at y 4330-4335, the stepped border x 4538-4570 and x 4707-4720 down column 3, x 4816-4822, 4855-4860 and 4966-4971 down column 4, y 3642-3648 and y 4212-4218 across column 4 blocks. Zoning letters R-1, R-2, R-3, C-2, C-1 and the R-3 lettering lying across column 3's left side at (4524-4560, 4400-4450) were ignored. No dead-end alleys met. Nothing here I could not read. Measured afterwards: along every typed side (box edges excluded), the outermost ink of the block's own line lies on the typed side at the median, within 1 px at 99.8% of 4,582 sample points, 2 px at most.
